title: Microengineering 3D Collagen Hydrogels with Long-Range Fiber Alignment
protocol: Fabricate the two-piece channel and modular platform base.
Mount a 250 µm thick PDMS sheet onto a plastic carrier sheet.
Razor-cut the microfluidic design using a craft cutter at a blade depth of 0.5 mm, speed of 1 cm/s, and high force.
Clean the microfluidic channel cutouts in an ultrasonic bath for 5 min.
Rinse the sonicated channels in deionized water.
Dry the rinsed channels on a clean hotplate at 100 °C for 5 min.
Store the cleaned and dried channels in a clean, covered Petri dish until use.
Fabricate the PDMS cover using a mold designed for the microfluidic channel cutout.
Affix a sheet of pressure-sensitive adhesive (PSA) to a 2.5 mm thick sheet of PMMA.
Laser cut the desired mold shape from the PMMA sheet.
Clean the laser-cut PMMA mold with a damp, lint-free wipe.
Attach the mold to a 100 mm diameter silicon wafer by pressing down firmly.
Prepare PDMS in a ratio of 10:1 (base:crosslinker).
Mix the PDMS vigorously for 1 min to ensure proper mixing.
Degas the mixture in a vacuum chamber to remove air bubbles.
Pour the degassed PDMS solution into the PMMA/silicon mold.
Cure the PDMS on a hotplate at 100 °C for 20 min.
Allow the cured PDMS to cool before removal from the mold.
Trim any excess PDMS with a razor blade.
Use a 1 mm diameter biopsy punch to create inlet and outlet holes on the PDMS covers.
Sonicate the cover in isopropanol (IPA) for 5 min.
Rinse with DI water.
Dry with a compressed air source.
Store in a clean, covered Petri dish.
Place the Petri dish in a UV sterilization chamber (uncovered) for 1 min to sterilize.
Cover and transfer to a biosafety cabinet (BSC).
Pipette 300 μL of 40 mg•mL-1 bovine serum albumin (BSA) in 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) onto the PDMS covers.
Spread the solution evenly using a pipette tip.
Place in a refrigerator at 4°C for at least 4 h before use.
Move the covers from the refrigerator into a BSC.
Wash 5x with 1x PBS.
Let them dry in air for 10 min.
Dilute a 25% glutaraldehyde solution to 5% in DI water.
Make 2 mL of 5% glutaraldehyde solution for each 24 mm x 50 mm coverslip.
For 24 mm x 24 mm or 22 mm x 22 mm coverslips, make 1 mL of 5% glutaraldehyde solution for each.
Clean the coverslips in a bath sonicator with IPA for 5 min.
Rinse off IPA from the coverslips using DI water until a smooth film of water is seen on the coverslip.
Dry the coverslips on a hot plate at 100 °C for 5 min.
Place dried coverslips into clean Petri dishes without overlapping.
Expose each coverslip to corona discharge for 1 min in a well-ventilated area or chemical hood.
Immerse each covered slip into APTES solution for 10 s within 5 min of corona exposure, ensuring the treated side faces upward and is submerged.
Dry the coverslips with compressed air after immersing them in acetone for 10 s.
Place dried coverslips back into Petri dishes with the treated side facing up.
Pipette 1 mL of glutaraldehyde solution onto each coverslip surface without spilling over the edge.
Add more glutaraldehyde solution if necessary to cover the surface completely, avoiding scratches with pipette tips.
Let the coverslips sit in contact with the solution for 30 min.
Rinse the coverslips with DI water for 20 s.
Dry the coverslips using compressed air.
Place the dried coverslips back in the Petri dishes, plasma treated side up.
Cut out designs from the PMMA layer using appropriate laser settings.
Wash the laser-cut part using soap and water to remove debris.
Push magnets into the laser-cut base by hand.
Use a soft hammer or screw-driver end to help push in the magnet if needed.
Attach the PSA sheet backing to a glutaraldehyde-treated coverslip with the functionalized side facing up.
Place the PDMS channel cutout into the cavity defined by the frame.
Press down with wide-tip tweezers to remove air bubbles and ensure conformal contact.
Place the BSA-treated channel cover on top of the channel cutout, ensuring the fluid inlet and outlet ports are aligned.
Calculate the volume of reagents required for preparing the COL1 solution on ice in the biosafety cabinet.
Add 416.67 µL of collagen to an empty 5 mL vial.
Add 429.16 µL of DI water to the vial.
Add 100 µL of 10x PBS to the vial.
Add 54.16 µL of 0.1 M NaOH to achieve a pH of 7 in the solution.
Adjust the pH to the desired level (typically between 7-9).
Use a displacement pipette to handle the COL1 solution.
Place a syringe pump, a chilled sterile syringe, chilled neutralized COL1 solution, and a sterile 20 G 90° angle tip Luer lock needle into a biosafety cabinet.
Load the COL1 solution into the syringe carefully.
Attach the 90° 20 G needle tip to the syringe.
Prime the needle with the COL1 solution.
Set the syringe pump to the required flow rate between 50-2,000 µL/min.
Place prepared PDMS channels on a lab jack and level them with the needle.
Insert the needle into the inlet port of the PDMS channel (wide side).
Inject the channel until a ~30 µL drop of COL1 collects on the outlet side.
Lower the lab jack gently to separate the needle from the newly filled channel.
Repeat steps 2.2.5-2.2.9 until all channels have been filled with COL1 solution.
Load the filled channels into Petri dishes alongside a clean, lint-free wipe saturated with DI water.
Cover the Petri dish and place it in the incubator at 37 °C and 95% humidity for 2 hours before the peel-off step.
Lift off the PDMS cover using tweezers to expose the polymerized COL1 gel.
Add 650 µL of EGM to the well after peeling off the cover.
Place the devices in the incubator at 37 °C and 95% humidity for a minimum of 4 hours to equilibrate the gel and media.
Discard the media in the T25 flask containing HUVECs.
Wash the cells twice with 1x PBS.
Add 1 mL of Trypsin to the flask and place it in the incubator at 37 °C and 95% humidity for 3 minutes.
Check the flask under a microscope after 3 minutes to ensure that the cells are completely detached from the surface.
Add 3 mL of EGM (with serum) to the flask to neutralize the trypsin.
Transfer the cell solution using a 5 mL pipette into a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the conical tube containing cells at 150 x g for 5 min.
Place the conical tube in the biosafety cabinet and discard the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of fresh culture media.
Add and mix 15 µL of trypan blue and 15 µL of the resuspended cell solution in a 1 mL conical tube.
Inject trypan blue and cell solution on both sides of a cell counting slide and insert the slide into a cell counting device.
Dilute the cell solution in endothelial growth media to the required concentration based on the cell concentration obtained from the cell counting device.
Aspirate the media on the engineered COL1 matrix.
Add the required volume of the cell solution onto the COL1 substrate.
Let the cells settle for a minimum of 4 h before imaging.
Aspirate the media from the cells.
Wash the cells three times with 1x PBS, using 500 µL in each wash.
Cover the cell layer with 4% paraformaldehyde for 15 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the paraformaldehyde and wash with 1x PBS Tween-20 for 5 min.
Permeabilize the cell membrane using 500 µL of 0.1% Triton-X solution in PBS for 15 min.
Wash with 1x PBS Tween-20 for 5 min.
Block non-specific binding sites with 500 µL of 4% BSA in PBS for 30 min at room temperature.
Dilute the phalloidin-actin fluorescent label solution in 4% BSA (1 µL stock in 400 µL BSA).
Aspirate the BSA solution, add the diluted phalloidin to the cells, and wait for 30 min at room temperature.
Dilute the nuclear stain in 4% BSA (1 µL in 500 µL).
Aspirate the phalloidin solution, add the working nuclear stain solution, and wait for 15 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the nuclear stain working solution.
Wash with PBS Tween-20 three times for 5 min each.
Replace with 1x PBS before imaging.
Image using an epifluorescent microscope using the FITC channel (ex 491 nm/em 516 nm) and DAPI channel (ex 360 nm/em 460 nm) with a 40x lens.
Image the collagen using a laser scanning confocal in reflectance mode using the 488 nm laser line at 15% power and 40x water-immersion objective.
